title: Rent Board Fee and Rent Increase License are easy to conflate
detail: They are separate obligations. The licence comes from Housing Inventory reporting; the fee is a per-unit annual payment (2026-2027: $59.00 per dwelling unit, due March 1). SF.gov states expressly that requesting a fee exemption does not satisfy Housing Inventory reporting, so an owner can be fee-paid and still unlicensed, or licensed and still owe the fee.

title: Two-unit owner-occupied exemption is conditional and unverified here
detail: AB 1482 exempts a two-unit structure only if the owner occupied one unit as a principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues in occupancy, and neither unit is an ADU/JADU. Whether the owner ever occupied a unit in this building was not supplied, so no exemption is asserted.

title: In-law or second structure on the lot changes coverage
detail: SF.gov states that a single-family dwelling with a LEGAL in-law unit is a two-unit building and is not exempt, that with an ILLEGAL in-law unit it is also a two-unit building and is not exempt UNLESS both units are rented together as a single tenancy, and that a single-family dwelling is not exempt if another residential structure is on the same lot. The owner described two units, which is consistent with Rent Ordinance coverage, but the official lot and building record was not supplied. Wording of this detail corrected 2026-11-08 - see F36.

title: QA correction: in-law-unit exemption wording was imprecise on this site
detail: The site previously summarised SF.gov as saying a dwelling with a legal or illegal in-law unit is not exempt 'unless both units are rented together as a single tenancy'. The page applies that exception only to an ILLEGAL in-law unit; a LEGAL in-law unit is not exempt at all. Found by line-by-line comparison on 2026-11-08 and corrected in S60, the Local Law row LOC-23, Q-20, F35 and the executive summary. No other finding or figure changed.

No date is chosen on this site; confirm with the Rent Board (311) before relying on either.

In the historical table the 7/03-6/04 row shows a $26.00 fee with a $21.50 tenant amount and the 7/01-6/02 row shows $16.00 with $16.00, while the form elsewhere says the tenant share is 50% (half again for residential-hotel guests). No value is inferred or corrected here; verify with the Rent Board before relying on any pre-2013 row.

title: No official statement links Rent Board Fee payment to licence validity

This is recorded as an absence of an official statement, not as an official confirmation that the two are unrelated.

title: Pending legislation could affect banked and capital-improvement increases
detail: On November 9, 2026 the Rent Board posted a notice about Board File 261020. The proposal would temporarily limit combined banked and capital-improvement increases to 10% per year; if enacted as currently proposed, it would apply to banked increases noticed on or after September 15, 2026 and capital-improvement increases based on petitions filed on or after that date. Legistar showed Pending Committee Action and no enactment on November 10. This is not current law and may change. A 90-day notice does not establish that an increase is lawful. Check the current status and seek advice before relying on a banked calculation or serving notice; its effect on either unit is unverified.

title: File 261020: proposed cap text clarified; application remains uncertain
detail: The Version 1 ordinance and legislative digest expressly define the 10% denominator as the lowest base rent in the preceding 12 months, cover specified banked notices and capital-improvement petitions on or after September 15, 2026, and specify an end of December 31, 2029 unless extended. The applicability date equals the introduction date and precedes the November 9 notice; the title and temporary notice do not establish a duration contradiction. The measure remains proposed, and its interaction with other increases and specific case facts requires review.

title: Notice worksheet: licence timing is effective-date based
detail: Rent Board Rule 13.14 uses the effective date of the increase, not the date of service, to test whether the landlord was licensed; confirming the licence before service is conservative practice only, not the stated legal test. Sources re-fetched 2026-11-10.

title: Notice worksheet: banking summary wording differs between SF guidance and Rule 4.12
detail: SF.gov banked-increase guidance says a skipped increase banks only after 24 full months without an increase, while Rule 4.12 of the Rules PDF describes a full 12 months from when an increase could have been imposed. Require the full rent history; no banking is inferred for either unit.

title: Notice worksheet: notice-nullity wording differs across official texts
detail: Sec. 37.3(b) requires a written breakdown of the increase components and makes a nonconforming increase null and void; Rule 4.12 requires the banked portion and dates. Include the full breakdown and banked dates conservatively; do not rely on limited exceptions without review.

title: Notice worksheet: Form 583 not verified as an annual-notice filing duty

No mandatory annual rent-increase notice template or annual filing duty was verified on the Forms Center (re-fetched 2026-11-10); keep a private service record.
